text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says region sliding towards extremism; says in CNN interview that PLO leader Yasser Arafat is despairing and Palestinians cannot continue to be humiliated without inviting a violent reaction.
- Crown Prince says that Israel's new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem loses the peace process its credibility.
- King Hussein and Arafat discuss on the phone the latest developments in the peace process.
- King may go to Morocco after end of his U.S. visit next week to attend meetings of the Quds (Jerusalem) committe, informed sources say.
- Parliament speaker expects the current final session of parliament to disband mid-next week, says its suspension would conform with its constitutional date.

- Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti says Jordan will not allow the Jerusalem issue to be tampered with; says Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's behaviour is a breach of signed peace accords.
- Prime minister says the human and legal dimensions of the case of the Hamas leader Abu Marzook held in a New York jail will be discussed with U.S. officials during the king's visit.
- Parliamentary deputies call for a review of the peace process and tie development of links with Israel to its adherence to peace accords.
- King Hussein and Crown Prince escalate the battle to save Jerusalem and peace.
- A seven-year-old girl's body swept by recent rains is found.
- Crown prince says that the right of Palestinian refugees to return or be compensated is not an issue of compromise.
- King: Jordan-Israel ties in most difficult period.
- King and queen arrive in Spain en route to U.S.
